ram:236e.comment: Accesses consecutive xdata bytes through one incremented pointer so that Keil keeps DPTR and emits INC DPTR between byte accesses instead of a separate MOV DPTR per byte. The second access to 0xa4ae goes through a fresh pointer cast, which reproduces the DPTR reload at that point.

ram:9f04.comment: Calls FUN_CODE_2820 (printf, declared `extern void FUN_CODE_2820(void *fmt, ...) large;`) with the generic code pointer 0xffdd52, passed as a `(void code *)` constant so that it is loaded into R3:R2:R1 (MOV R3,#0xff; MOV R2,#0xdd; MOV R1,#0x52) before the LCALL.

ram:b06f.comment: Writes 0xFF to xdata register 0xd910 and related xdata registers via MOV DPTR,#addr; MOV A,#imm; MOVX @DPTR,A, clears a bdata bit (sbit), and ends with a tail call to FUN_CODE_cd07 emitted as LJMP. The registers must be declared xdata so Keil uses MOVX @DPTR addressing instead of direct addressing.
ram:b06f.name: FUN_CODE_b06f

ram:b192.comment: Busy-waits on bit 1 of an xdata status register, compiled as ANL A,#2 / JNZ (an integer comparison in source, not a bit test that would emit JB ACC.1), then performs a dummy read of xdata 0xf1c0 whose value is stored to R4 before A is cleared, so the read value must be used in source.
ram:b192.name: FUN_CODE_b192

ram:bbca.comment: The function takes two byte parameters: a mask and a value. For each of the 7 low bits set in the mask, it sets bit 7 of the corresponding high register (0xF181, 0xF183, ..., 0xF18D) and writes the value byte to the adjacent low register (0xF180, 0xF182, ..., 0xF18C). The structure is a sequence of independent if-blocks in ascending bit order, each performing a read-modify-write on the high register followed by a write to the low register. The mask is kept in R6 (matching the target's `MOV R6,R7` at entry) and the value in R5, matching the register usage in the firmware's byte pattern.
ram:bbca.name: FUN_CODE_bbca

ram:bde9.comment: Takes a bitmask sel (R7) and a value val (R5). Clears the LSB of val (keeps bits 1-7), then for each set bit in sel writes (current_value & 1) | val to the matching XDATA register: bit 0 -> 0xF040, bit 1 -> 0xF048, bit 2 -> 0xF090, bit 3 -> 0xF098, bit 4 -> 0xF0A2, bit 5 -> 0xF0BF, bit 6 -> 0xF147, bit 7 -> 0xF01B. The MOV R4,AR7 copy in the target is how Keil copies the first parameter.
ram:bde9.name: FUN_CODE_bde9

ram:c085.comment: The function reads two xdata registers at 0xf021 and 0xf022, masks each with 0xF0, and ORs in a shared value from 0xa1e7, then writes back to the respective registers. The main uncertainty is whether the value at 0xa1e7 is read once or twice — the assembly reads it once into R6 and reuses it for both OR operations, which matches the C above.
ram:c085.name: FUN_CODE_c085

ram:c278.comment: Clears bit 0 of eight xdata registers, one per set bit of the byte parameter (copied to R5): bit 0 -> 0xf040, bit 1 -> 0xf048, bit 2 -> 0xf090, bit 3 -> 0xf098, bit 4 -> 0xf0a2, bit 5 -> 0xf0bf, bit 6 -> 0xf147, bit 7 -> 0xf01b. Each bit test is followed by a read-modify-write of its register; `param_1 & (1 << n)` and `(param_1 >> n) & 1` compile identically.
ram:c278.name: FUN_CODE_c278

ram:cfe7.comment: Accesses IDATA byte DAT_INTMEM_50 at 0x50 through MOV R0,#0x50 indirect addressing. The variable is defined (not declared extern) as unsigned char idata DAT_INTMEM_50 _at_ 0x50, since Keil rejects extern with _at_.
ram:cfe7.name: FUN_CODE_cfe7

ram:d13a.comment: Makes five calls that pass a byte in R7, a byte in R5 and a 16-bit word in R2:R3 (R2 high, R3 low): (0x00, 0x80, 0x01c2), (0x10, 0x00, 0x0640), (0x20, 0x80, 0x0002), (0x30, 0x80, 0x001c), (0x50, 0x80, 0x0136). The callee prototype is (unsigned char, unsigned char, unsigned int).
ram:d13a.name: FUN_CODE_d13a

ram:d24a.comment: Interrupt-style function using register bank 3 (`using 3`, MOV PSW,#0x18). It tests bit 7 of DAT_EXTMEM_d90b with the sequence ANL A,#0x80; XRL A,#0x80; JNZ, which requires the source form `if ((DAT_EXTMEM_d90b & 0x80) ^ 0x80)` rather than a plain bit test (which compiles to XRL/JB ACC.7).
ram:d24a.name: FUN_CODE_d24a

ram:d5c8.comment: This function writes a constant to one xdata register, clears bit 7 of another, then branches on whether a third register equals 0x20 (space): if equal, it keeps only bit 0 of a fourth register; otherwise keeps the low nibble. It then sets bit 0 of a fifth register and tail-calls `FUN_CODE_daad`. The main uncertainty is whether the final call is truly a tail call (LJMP) rather than a call followed by return; the assembly uses LJMP, so this should match.
ram:d5c8.name: FUN_CODE_d5c8
